minutes.headline: Sewer Commission adopted a new deduct meter policy, approved the pump station contract, and passed a counsel-access policy.
minutes.summary: The commission closed a second public hearing and approved the renamed deduct meter policy, then approved the 2020 pump station operations and maintenance contract. Members discussed a gap in the regulations about who locates sewer tie-in connections, and agreed to add a paragraph. A proposed town counsel access policy was changed from requiring permission to requiring notification and then voted on, over objection from one member.

what_happened.line: The Sewer Commission closed a public hearing and approved the renamed deduct meter policy by roll call.
The commission accepted the 2020 operations and maintenance contract for the pump stations by roll call.
Members agreed that the business manager and DPW director will draft a paragraph on who is responsible for locating sewer tie-in connections.
A town counsel access policy was changed from requiring permission to requiring notification and put to a vote; the outcome was not audible in the recording.
The warrant for the next meeting closes September 29, and the first quarter commitment was put to a vote that was not audible.

why_it_matters: The deduct meter policy and the tie-in paragraph set who pays for and who locates sewer connections, which touches homeowners who install meters or connect to the sewer.
The pump station contract and the first quarter commitment affect sewer operating costs and the billing that flows into sewer bills.
watch_next: Next meeting, September 29: the draft tie-in paragraph, the special town meeting warrant and the budget review.
The recording does not make clear whether the counsel access policy and the first quarter commitment passed; the approved minutes should settle it.
